about.title: Rancho Palos Verdes Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Rancho Palos Verdes sits on terraced bluffs above the Pacific, and that terrain shapes daily life here — uneven walkways near ocean lookouts, sloped parking areas along Palos Verdes Drive S, and steps or landscaping features at hillside properties. When a property owner fails to maintain those surfaces, fix a known spill, or light a dim stairwell, a routine walk can end in a serious fall. California premises liability law doesn't hand injured people anything automatically; it requires showing the owner knew or reasonably should have known about the hazard and didn't address it in time. That's why documenting the scene matters so much, and why acting before surveillance footage gets erased matters even more. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we're a free service that connects people hurt in falls around Rancho Palos Verdes with an independent attorney who can evaluate the notice question, gather evidence, and explain your options without any upfront cost to you.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney About Notice and Evidence

items.title: Proving the Owner Knew or Should Have Known
items.desc: California law requires showing the property owner had notice of the hazard and failed to fix or warn about it. An attorney can help gather maintenance logs, complaint records, or photos that speak to how long the hazard existed.

items.title: Surveillance Video Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many properties overwrite security footage within days or weeks. Getting a preservation request out quickly can be the difference between having video evidence and having none.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce, Not Erase, a Claim
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, so even if you're found partly responsible for a fall, you may still be entitled to recover a reduced amount. An attorney can help present the facts fairly instead of letting an insurer assign blame unchecked.

items.question: I slipped near a coastal trail or overlook in Rancho Palos Verdes — who's responsible?
items.answer: It depends on who owns or maintains that property, which could be a private business, an HOA, or a public entity. Claims against public entities in California often carry a much shorter filing deadline than the general two-year window, so it helps to get that identified early. An attorney can help sort out ownership and the applicable deadline.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in California?
items.answer: Generally, you have two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit for a premises liability injury. That window can be shorter if a government-owned property was involved. It's best not to wait, since evidence like video and witness memory fades quickly.

items.question: What if I can't prove the property owner knew about the hazard?
items.answer: You don't need a written record to establish notice — evidence like how long a substance was on the floor, prior complaints, or the condition's obviousness can all help show the owner should have known. This is often the most contested part of a premises liability claim, which is why documentation and quick evidence-gathering matter. An independent attorney can help evaluate what you have and what else might be available.
